title: CastillosBurstVEP40
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from a code-modulated Visual Evoked Potential (c-VEP) brain-computer interface study introducing an innovative 'Burst c-VEP' paradigm. Data were collected from 12 healthy participants using 32-channel EEG at 500 Hz during a reactive BCI task with visual stimuli presented at 2-4 Hz. The study investigates the effects of stimulus pattern (burst vs. m-sequence codes) and amplitude depth (100% vs. 40%) on classification performance and user experience, demonstrating that burst c-VEP achieves high accuracy (90.5-95.6%) with reduced calibration requirements and improved visual comfort.
methods_description: EEG data acquired from 12 healthy participants (mean age 30.6±7.1 years) using a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system at 500 Hz sampling rate with standard 10-20 electrode montage (reference: FCz, ground: FPz). Factorial experimental design manipulating stimulus pattern (burst codes: 50ms flashes at 2-4 Hz; m-sequences: ~10 Hz pseudo-random) and amplitude depth (100% or 40%). Each participant completed 15 blocks of 4 trials per condition (240 total trials). Stimuli presented on Dell P2419HC display (1920×1080, 60 Hz). Online 50 Hz line noise filtering applied. Classification performed using convolutional neural networks with EEG2Code bitwise decoding.
